Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the EnergiCore Utilities Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Lisa Chen, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to EnergiCore Utilities Inc.'s Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; and Mike Harlan, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Lisa, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by strong operational performance in our generation fleet, continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio, effective cost management, and progress on our infrastructure investments.

Let me provide some more detail on these four key aspects.

Starting with strong operational performance across our generation fleet. Reliability remains the foundation of our operations as we balance affordability, decarbonization, and dependable service amid growing complexity in power generation and transmission and distribution. Our system-wide SAIDI for the quarter stood at 62.4 minutes, reflecting a 14% year-over-year improvement from 72.6 minutes, surpassing our target of 68 minutes. Year-to-date, SAIDI is 142.8 minutes, down 11% from last year, on pace for a full-year range of 185 to 195 minutes, with a five-year compound annual improvement of 8.2% that compares favorably to NERC peers like Duke Energy or Evergy. SAIFI improved to 0.89 interruptions per customer in the quarter, a 17% decline from 1.07, and 2.12 year-to-date versus 2.48 prior year. These gains exclude major events, with ex-major event day SAIDI at a record 28.1 minutes. We'll dive deeper into these metrics during Q&A.

Next, our continued growth in the renewable energy portfolio, which is central to accelerating the clean energy transition, bolstering grid reliability and resilience, and pursuing customer-focused expansion to address rising electrification needs. We're progressing toward 40% carbon-free generation by 2030 from today's 28%, having added 1.2 gigawatts of renewables year-to-date, 15% ahead of our annual 2-gigawatt target. In this quarter, we commissioned 450 megawatts of utility-scale solar at the Desert Bloom project in ERCOT, utilizing First Solar's efficient thin-film modules under 15-year power purchase agreements with investment-grade buyers, including a hyperscaler for 200 megawatts at $28 per megawatt-hour, with capacity factors over 28% thanks to bifacial technology and Nextracker single-axis systems. Wind repowering at Prairie Winds in MISO, upgrading to Vestas V150 turbines for 300 megawatts, lifted output 25% and asset life by 15 years. This supports our $3.5 billion renewables investment through 2027, financed 60% by retained earnings, 30% green bonds, and 10% tax equity, displacing 1.8 million metric tons of CO2 yearly toward our SBTi-validated 50% Scope 1 and 2 reduction goal by 2030. Battery storage advancements include 250 megawatts over 1,000 megawatt-hours at Ironclad in PJM, co-located with gas assets for 4-hour duration arbitrage yielding $45 million this quarter at $150 per megawatt-hour peaks, lifting fleet capacity factor to 62%. Upcoming 500-megawatt projects in CAISO and SPP target late 2025 operations with DOE support. On resilience, $450 million year-to-date in upgrades like 200 miles of 3M composite reconductoring cut SAIDI 18%, while our GE Vernova ADMS covers 85% of the grid for DER management, integrating 50 megawatts of customer solar and EV chargers, with virtual power plant growth up 35% quarter-over-quarter. Load served rose 7.5% to 45 terawatt-hours, driven by 22% EV growth and 500 megawatts from gigafactories, plus a $200 million rebate program capturing 15% DER market share. We're pursuing accretive M&A, like a letter of intent for 400 megawatts of wind at 9 times EV/EBITDA. These efforts drove adjusted ROE to 11.2%, FFO of $1.4 to $1.5 billion for the year, and a 4.2% dividend yield with 5% hikes. Long-term, net-zero by 2045 includes 50% renewables by 2030, 5 gigawatts storage by 2035, and a 100-megawatt hydrogen pilot blending 20% into GE turbines by 2026. Mitigated risks include 80% locked PPAs and IRA benefits worth $250 million this year.

On effective cost management, we've maintained discipline through hedging 92% of 2024 exposure at $40 per megawatt-hour floors against gas volatility, optimizing our 8.5-gigawatt fleet at 78% capacity factor, and leveraging automation to save on crew hours while addressing O&M upticks from outages now resolved.

Finally, progress on infrastructure investments supports steady rate base expansion at a 5.7% compound annual growth rate to $42.5 billion by 2028, driven by transmission and distribution modernization, clean energy adds, and portfolio tweaks, with key assumptions around regulatory approvals, 3.5% capex inflation, and 3% load growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to discuss the financials.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. For the Q3 2024 quarter, we reported earnings per share of $1.42 and revenue of $3.82 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Let me delve into the revenue breakdown by our regulated and unregulated segments, which highlights the resilience and growth potential in the shifting power generation environment.

Total revenues rose 6.2% year-over-year to $3.82 billion, exceeding our guidance midpoint by 150 basis points. Regulated revenues from transmission and distribution operations under FERC formula rates and state public utility commission cases made up $2.58 billion, or 67.5%, with unregulated at $1.24 billion or 32.5%. Year-to-date, the mix is 68% regulated to 32% unregulated, aligning with full-year guidance of 67% to 69% regulated.

Regulated grew 4.1% to $2.58 billion, supported by 2.8% weather-normalized retail load growth from data centers and electrification. In the Northeast, akin to Eversource areas, load increased 3.2% with ISO-NE capacity at $7.50 per kilowatt-month, up 15%, flowing through rate riders. We recovered $450 million in capex via formula true-ups, 85% CWIP for grid hardening, earning 10.35% ROE on a $28 billion rate base, with AFUDC contributing 22 cents to EPS. Highlights include the $1.2 billion Advanced Grid Modernization Program with 5,000 miles of fiber reconductoring and 1.2 gigawatts battery interconnection in PJM, enabling 450 megawatts behind-the-meter solar and storage, plus $15 million from FERC Order 2222 virtual power plants. Midwest saw 2.5% MISO South load growth, and Texas ERCOT benefited from a $120 million rate case settlement for storm recovery and EV infrastructure.

Unregulated revenues jumped 12.7% to $1.24 billion on strong markets, with realized energy margins at $42 per megawatt-hour versus $35 last year, from PJM LMPs of $55 and ERCOT $75 amid heat and nuclear performance. Our 8.5-gigawatt fleet—45% gas CCCT, 30% nuclear, 25% renewables—ran at 78% capacity factor. Renewables delivered $520 million or 42%, up 18% on wind factors for 2.8 gigawatts onshore and solar PTCs under IRA; batteries captured $28 per megawatt-hour spreads; thermal sales $480 million or 39% with 92% hedged; trading $240 million or 19% including $65 million nodal deals in CAISO.

This 'regulated stability, unregulated upside' supports 85% hedged 2025 exposure and 65% 2026, plus a $2.5 billion renewables pipeline with 1.5 gigawatts solar-plus-storage PPAs for hyperscalers at 15-20% IRRs. We've inked 800 megawatts wheeling for data centers backed by nuclear. EBITDA margins dipped 200 basis points to 28% from $80 million nuclear O&M now fixed and $50 million New York provisions, but diversification shines with regulated funding 70% of $4.2 billion annual capex and 12% unregulated free cash flow yield. Q4 regulated $2.65 to $2.70 billion, unregulated $1.35 to $1.45 billion, full-year consolidated $15.2 to $15.5 billion, targeting 7-9% EPS CAGR.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $1.05 billion, primarily focused on grid modernization and renewable expansion. Building on that, our rate base growth outlook to $42.5 billion by end-2028 at 5.7% CAGR adds $10.4 billion net, 60% T&D, 30% clean generation, 10% AFUDC at 6.8% cost of capital. T&D contributes $6.2 billion via $1.8 billion reconductoring like 3M ACCR on 345 kV lines boosting ampacity 60%, $900 million grid-enhancing tech from Smart Wires for 15% capacity lift, and $1.2 billion substations for 3.5% load growth including 2.2 gigawatts data centers. Clean energy adds $3.1 billion: 1.5 gigawatts solar like 400-megawatt Sundown at $28 per megawatt-hour LCOE, 300 megawatts Midwest wind, 1.2 gigawatts/4.8 gigawatt-hours storage like Pine Ridge for PJM services. Generation nets $1.1 billion, retiring 600 megawatts coal for $350 million to fund CCUS on 800-megawatt cycles for 45Q credits. Southeast (65% rate base) grows 6.5% CAGR with CWIP approvals; South Carolina 5%; Midwest 4.2%. Assumptions: 90% capex approvals, 70/30 debt-equity, 3.5% inflation, 3% load, $3.25 Henry Hub gas, no recession. Risks like supply chains or FERC 1920 offset by IRA upsides. This flywheel drives 6-8% EPS growth and 10% shareholder returns.

We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Paul Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Paul Thompson: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for progress on strategic initiatives and long-term goals?

Johnathan Hale: Certainly, Paul. As detailed earlier, we're advancing rapidly on clean energy with renewables ahead of plan, resilience investments cutting outages, and customer growth from electrification, all backed by our capex and financing strategy to hit net-zero ahead of peers while growing earnings steadily.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez: What is your outlook for unregulated segment performance?

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, Maria. As I outlined, we see strong tailwinds from market dynamics and hedging, with Q4 guidance at $1.35 to $1.45 billion and full-year unregulated growth of 10-14%, supported by our pipeline and data center deals.

Operator: Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Greenleaf Capital. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thanks, and good morning, team. Strong quarter on the reliability front—congrats on beating your SAIDI target. Can you drill down into the SAIDI and SAIFI metrics, system performance trends, and how that's tying into your capex strategy amid the DER boom and weather volatility? Regional color would be great too.

Mike Harlan: Thanks, Alex. Great question—reliability is the bedrock of our business at EnergiCore Utilities Inc., especially as we navigate the trilemma of affordability, decarbonization, and rock-solid service in a power generation and T&D world that's getting more complex. Let me unpack our Q3 2024 and year-to-date performance on SAIDI and SAIFI, weave in system-wide trends, and connect it to our strategic levers. We serve 4.2 million metered customers across 65,000 miles of distribution and 12,000 miles of transmission in Midwest, Southeast, and Northeast territories.

Headline figures: Q3 system-wide SAIDI at 62.4 minutes—14% better than 72.6 in Q3 2023, beating our 68-minute target. Year-to-date SAIDI 142.8 minutes, down 11% from 160.2, tracking 185-195 full-year with 8.2% five-year CAGR improvement topping NERC medians around 210 for peers. SAIFI Q3 at 0.89 per customer, 17% below 1.07; year-to-date 2.12 versus 2.48, beating 2.30 target with -6.5% five-year CAGR. Excluding three major event days—like Midwest ice storms at 1.2 inches on 69kV and Southeast hurricane remnants—Q3 SAIDI was 28.1 minutes, our best. CAIDI down to 67.4 minutes per event, MAIFI improved 9% to 2.45 via SEL-751 relays on 85% substations.

Regionally: Midwest (Illinois/Missouri, 2.1 million customers) SAIDI 55.2 minutes, 22% better than Ameren peers, thanks to 28,000 miles ROW trimming with LiDAR drones and Trimble AI, cutting tree outages 31%. Southeast (Georgia/Carolinas, 1.4 million) 78.6 minutes from weather but 12% above Southern averages; ex-MED 32 minutes matching Georgia Power. Northeast (Pennsylvania/New York, 700k) 52.1 minutes aided by 15 miles 138kV undergrounding, reducing wind faults 25%.

System performance: GE DMS/ADMS with Esri achieved 92% first-time fault isolation via FLISR on 72% feeders. Outage causes: weather 42% (down from hardened poles—4,200 composites), equipment 28% (ABB ML on 1.2 million SCADA points), vegetation 30%. Five-year SAIDI down 32% despite 15% load growth—EVs 8% peak, data centers 12%. Renewables (2.8 gigawatts solar, 1.2 gigawatts wind including Rattlesnake Flats) added voltage events, countered by 450 megawatt-hours Fluence BESS and S&C VVO on 65% feeders maintaining 95% voltage bands.

Financially, regulators reward it—a 50 basis point ROE adder unlocked $45 million. Capex $1.2 billion year-to-date, 28% reliability including $320 million Landis+Gyr AMI for 88% CSAT; OMS saved $28 million. Outlook: 170-180 SAIDI, 1.95-2.05 SAIFI normalized. Initiatives: $750 million resilience Phase 2 with micro-PMUs, NextEra hybrid, Overstory AI for 100% ROW, Sunrun VPP for 200 megawatts and 15% SAIFI cut.

In short, our system is antifragile, fueling rate recovery, premium loads, and clean growth ahead of Exelon peers.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning EnergiCore Utilities Inc. for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in EnergiCore Utilities Inc.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
